question: Who among the following was the founder of the slave dynasty who was the army commander of Muhammad Ghori earlier ?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Qutbuddin Aibak**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Qutbuddin Aibak was the founder of the Slave dynasty in India, which is also known as the Mamluk dynasty.
 
• He was initially a slave who rose to the rank of an army commander under Muhammad Ghori, a prominent ruler of the Ghurid Empire.
 
• After the death of Muhammad Ghori, Qutbuddin Aibak established himself as an independent ruler in Delhi in 1206.
 
• Qutbuddin Aibak is also known for commissioning the construction of the Qutub Minar, a UNESCO World Heritage Site in Delhi.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Slave Dynasty (Mamluk Dynasty)**

 
 
• The Slave dynasty, also known as the Mamluk dynasty, was the first of the Delhi Sultanates, ruling from 1206 to 1290.
 
• It was founded by Qutbuddin Aibak, who was originally a slave purchased by Muhammad Ghori, and later rose to become his trusted general and governor of Indian territories.
 
• The term "Mamluk" means "owned" or "slave" in Arabic, indicating that many rulers of this dynasty were originally slaves.
 
• The Slave dynasty contributed significantly to the establishment of Muslim rule in India and laid the foundation for subsequent dynasties.
 
 
 
• **Muhammad Ghori**
 
 
• Muhammad Ghori was a ruler of the Ghurid Empire who played a crucial role in the expansion of Muslim rule into the Indian subcontinent.
 
• He conducted several military campaigns in northern India, defeating various Rajput kings and other local rulers.
 
• His notable victory at the Second Battle of Tarain in 1192 against Prithviraj Chauhan paved the way for Muslim dominance in northern India.
 
• Muhammad Ghori's conquests laid the groundwork for the establishment of the Delhi Sultanate.
 
 
 
• **Qutub Minar**
 
 
• The Qutub Minar is a minaret that forms part of the Qutub complex, a UNESCO World Heritage Site in Delhi, India.
 
• It was commissioned by Qutbuddin Aibak in 1192 and completed by his successor, Iltutmish.
 
• The minaret is 73 meters tall, making it the tallest brick minaret in the world.
 
• The Qutub Minar is an excellent example of Indo-Islamic architecture, featuring intricate carvings and inscriptions in Arabic.
